title: Ctrl-C recorded as task failure

         tid = task["id"]

-        except BaseException as e:   # noqa: BLE001

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -57,7 +57,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: The timeout handler only returns a CompletedProcess when stdout has content. If the subprocess wrote only to stderr before timing out, the condition `if str(stdout).strip():` evaluates to False, causing it to raise ProcTimeout and discard the stderr data. Adding `or str(stderr).strip()` ensures any captured output (stdout or stderr) is returned to the caller instead of being lost.
